jsonld.name: Full English Breakfast Pizza
jsonld.description: The full English on a pizza base: a thin, oven-blistered crust spread with a tomato-and-brown-sauce base, loaded with sausage crumbles, bacon, mushrooms, and black pudding, and finished — after the bake — with eggs cracked on in the last minutes so the yolks arrive runny and the whites set into the pizza's own sauce. It is the dish that sounds like a stunt and eats like a tradition-in-waiting: every component is already a pizza topping in disguise, and the egg-on-pizza idea belongs to half the world's breakfast cultures already. The technique has two rules that make or break it: the base sauce is cooked thick (a watery base floods the crust), and the eggs go on late and cool — cracked onto the pizza for the final 4 minutes only, so the whites set while the crust's bottom stays crisp and the yolks stay molten.

100 g mature Cheddar or mozzarella, grated (a 50/50 mix is the house blend)
2 slices (100 g) black pudding, optional extra for the finish
Black pepper; brown sauce drizzle for the slices

skeleton:
Full English Breakfast Pizza

British · Medium · Serves 2–3

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English on a pizza base: a thin, oven-blistered crust spread with a tomato-and-brown-sauce base, loaded with sausage crumbles, bacon, mushrooms, and black pudding, and finished — after the bake — with eggs cracked on in the last minutes so the yolks arrive runny and the whites set into the pizza's own sauce. It is the dish that sounds like a stunt and eats like a tradition-in-waiting: every component is already a pizza topping in disguise, and the egg-on-pizza idea belongs to half the world's breakfast cultures already. The technique has two rules that make or break it: the base sauce is cooked thick (a watery base floods the crust), and the eggs go on late and cool — cracked onto the pizza for the final 4 minutes only, so the whites set while the crust's bottom stays crisp and the yolks stay molten.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The dough

The base sauce

The toppings

To finish

- **The dough needs its hour:** mix, knead 8 minutes, rise 60 minutes until doubled — a pizza dough short on rise bakes to cracker and sogs at the first sauce. Start it first; everything else happens in its rise. - **The oven as hot as it goes** — a pizza stone or upturned baking tray preheated at 240 °C (or higher) for 30 minutes. The base needs the stone's blast to crisp before the toppings wet it. - **Every topping pre-cooked and dry.** Raw sausage on a 10-minute pizza is raw sausage at the end; wet mushrooms are a flooded base. The components cook while the dough rises; the pizza assembles in minutes. - The eggs cracked into cups, ready for the oven-door moment.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Dough: full hour's rise; shaped thin with a 2 cm bare rim.
  • Sauce: reduced to mound-on-spoon; toppings cooked, cooled, and dry.
  • Bake: stone-hot, 8 minutes, eggs on at the door, 3–4 more to glossy-set whites.
  • The base crisp at the slice — the flood test passed.

Full English Breakfast Pizza

Prep: 25 minutes, plus 1 hour dough rise · Cook: 15 minutes · Total: About 1 hour 40 minutes · Serves 2–3

Ingredients

The dough

  • 250 g strong white bread flour
  • 5 g instant yeast
  • 5 g fine sea salt
  • 5 ml / 5 g olive oil
  • 170 ml / 170 g warm water

The base sauce

  • 100 g passata, simmered 8 minutes until thick
  • 10 g brown breakfast sauce
  • 1 g smoked paprika
  • 1 g salt

The toppings

  • 2 pork sausages (160 g), skins removed, crumbled and browned
  • 3 rashers (150 g) back bacon, chopped and cooked to just-under
  • 80 g black pudding, crumbled and seared
  • 80 g chestnut mushrooms, sliced and browned dry
  • 100 g mature Cheddar or mozzarella, grated (a 50/50 mix is the house blend)
  • 2 large eggs (110 g)
  • 2 slices (100 g) black pudding, optional extra for the finish

To finish

  • 5 g chopped chives or parsley
  • Black pepper; brown sauce drizzle for the slices

Instructions

  1. **Mix, knead, rise.** Combine the flour, yeast, and salt, add the oil and water, and knead 8 minutes to a smooth, elastic ball. Oil a bowl, cover the dough, and rise 1 hour until doubled. Checkpoint — the dough domes and jiggles, and a poked dent fills slowly — the standard proof. This is also when the toppings and sauce cook.
  2. **Simmer the sauce and cook the toppings.** Reduce the passata with the brown sauce, paprika, and salt for 8 minutes until it mounds on a spoon — thick enough to spread as a layer, not a puddle. Brown the crumbled sausage 6 minutes; add the bacon for the last 3; sear the black pudding crumb alongside; brown the mushrooms separately until dry. Cool everything. Checkpoint — the sauce holds a spatula trail; the toppings sit in their bowl with no juice pooling at the bottom. The brown sauce in the base is the pizza's full-English signature — tomato's fruit with the breakfast table's spice underneath.
  3. **Shape and top.** Heat the stone at 240 °C-plus for 30 minutes. Stretch or roll the dough to a 30 cm round on a floured peel or upturned tray. Spread the sauce to within 2 cm of the edge, scatter the cheese, then the sausage, bacon, pudding, and mushrooms evenly — no mountains, everything one layer deep. Checkpoint — an even, flat-topped disc where no component towers — tall toppings slide, and the eggs need level ground. The 2 cm sauce-free rim is the crust's handle.
  4. **Bake 8 minutes, eggs on, 4 more.** Slide the pizza onto the stone and bake 8 minutes, until the crust's rim has puffed and blisters. Pull the pizza out (peel under, confident), make two wells in the toppings with the back of a spoon, and slide an egg into each. Back in the oven for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks still run. Checkpoint — whites set opaque but glossy-topped, yolks domed and liquid; the crust's edge deep-gold with char freckles at its blisters. The eggs' 4 minutes is the window — check at 3, and remember the yolk keeps cooking on the hot pizza for the next five minutes of serving.
  5. **Finish at the board.** The pizza to a board, chives and pepper over, and cut into wedges with the eggs' yolks breaking across the slices — each slice sauced by design. Checkpoint — the eating test: crust crackles and chars at the rim, the base holds crisp under its toppings, and the first slice carries egg, sausage, bacon, and pudding with the sauce's brown-sauce undertone. The full English and the pizza have signed their treaty.

Finish & Plate

Cut at the board, eaten with hands, brown sauce for the crust's edge. The breakfast pizza's role is the brunch crowd's centrepiece — halve the dough and run two pizzas for four — and the leftover wedges are the lunchbox's best cold slice, though the yolk's memory will be the only runny thing left.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Soggy-centred baseThin sauce, wet toppings, or cool ovenReduce the sauce; dry the mushrooms; stone at maximum for 30 minutes
Eggs overcookedOn from the start, or left too longThe door-crack at 8 minutes; 3–4 minutes with a check
Toppings slid off at the sliceOverloaded or no level wellsOne flat layer; wells for the eggs
Cracker crustDough under-risen or rolled too thinThe full hour; 3–4 mm centre thickness

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The dough keeps 3 days refrigerated** (its slow cold rise improves it); toppings and sauce hold 3 days each — assembly is 10 minutes on the morning. Baked, it is a same-day dish; the egg condemns the leftovers to the lunchbox. - **Variation — the hash brown base:** a wrung-potato crust par-baked 12 minutes, then topped — the gluten-free direction and the potato-first restructure. - **Variation — the vegan bake:** the vegan master's tofu scramble cracked on in spoonfuls for the final 5 minutes — the eggs' slot filled without the clock's cruelty. - **The format trilogy:** pie (custard), pizza (flat), pasty (sealed) — three baked full Englishes, each solving water, crust, and egg in its own dialect.

methodSteps.chefsNote: the late-egg method is the record's whole technique: eggs on from the start give you 12-minute yolks — chalk and rubber — because the white's 4-minute set and the yolk's liquid window cannot survive a pizza's full bake. Cracking them on at the door, into wells pressed into the toppings, gives each egg a cradle that holds it level and sets it in exactly the time the crust needs to finish. It is the same timing logic as the hash's lid-set eggs and the baked-eggs' pan-finish: the egg's clock always runs separately from everything else's.

methodSteps.chefsNote: the brown-sauce-in-the-base is this pizza's full-English signature and it works because brown sauce and reduced tomato share a vinegar backbone — the one seasons the other rather than fighting it. Start at 10 g of brown sauce per 100 g of passata and taste after the simmer: the base should read as tomato-with-a-past, not as brown sauce with tomato in it. Overdose and the bake amplifies the tamarind; underdose and you have made a breakfast-flavoured margherita, which is a different and more apologetic dish.
